title: DynaCell reveals trade-offs between spatial and phenotype fidelity in live-cell virtual staining
summary: The DynaCell suite compared regression and generative virtual-staining baselines on 3D time-lapse data across three cell types, two microscopes, four organelles, and three perturbation states. Regression baselines better localized organelles, while the generative baseline better captured phenotype distributions across cells. The result is limited to the evaluated cells, models, and imaging conditions.
ai_technology: Regression and generative image-to-image models for 3D virtual staining
organization: Biohub; University of California, San Francisco

evidence.tested: The evaluation suite compared 3D time-lapse virtual-staining baselines over three cell types, two microscopes, four organelles, and three perturbation states, using pixel-fidelity, organelle-segmentation, and single-cell phenotype metrics. Regression models better localized organelles; the generative model better captured phenotype distributions.
evidence.unknown: The comparison is limited to the evaluated data, models, and imaging conditions; performance for other cell types or downstream biological uses is not established.
evidence.ai_role: Regression and generative models predicted fluorescence-like images from label-free live-cell images; the study compared their spatial and phenotype-level performance.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
